FEBRUARY 8, 1945: The President of the United States of America, authorized by Act of Congress July 9, 1918, takes pleasure in presenting the Silver Star to Major James E. Foxx, United States Army, for gallantry in action while serving with Headquarters, 37th Infantry Division, in action against enemy forces at Luzon, Philippine Islands. On 8 and 9 February 1945, when an infantry regiment was making an amphibious crossing of the Pasig River in the vicinity of the Malacanan Palace in Manila. Major Foxx was charged with the responsibility for the proper employment of all available boats. The enemy was tenaciously contesting the crossing and engaged the Americans with artillery, mortar, rocket, and small arms fire. Placing himself on the near shore where he could exercise proper control of the boats utilized in the crossing, Major Foxx, although wounded by fragments of a mortar shell, remained at his post of duty for a period of 30 hours and rendered outstanding services in the successful crossing of the assaulting troops. On 17 February 1945, at the Philippine General Hospital in Manila, Major Foxx was placed in charge of all transportation utilized in the evacuation of 7,000 civilians who had been imprisoned within the walls of the institution. The Japanese were occupying neighboring gun emplacements and sporadic fire was falling on the troops engaged in the rescue of the Hospital inmates. In order to adequately supervise his vehicles, Major Foxx occupied a position with the foremost infantry elements and, disregarding the constant danger of enemy fire, displayed outstanding efficiency and untiring devotion to duty in accomplishing a difficult assignment. His gallant actions and dedicated devotion to duty, without regard for his own life, were in keeping with the highest traditions of military service and reflect great credit upon himself, his unit, and the United States Army.
